reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel sigma algebra. Give E x E the standard product max norm, so the distance between (x,p) and (y,q) is max(norm(x-y), norm(p-q)). For every pair of measures nu and reference on E x E, every xstar in E, and every r, Mx, Mp in R, assume that z -> norm(z.1-xstar)^2 and z -> norm(z.2)^2 are integrable with respect to reference, with respective integrals at most Mx and Mp. Assume also that the square of the ordinary Samplinglib wassersteinDistance(nu, reference), calculated using that product metric, is at most ENNReal.ofReal(r^2). Then z -> norm(z.1-xstar)^2 + norm(z.2)^2 is integrable with respect to nu, and its integral with respect to nu is at most 2*(Mx+Mp)+4*r^2. Here norm is the inner-product norm on E, R denotes the real numbers, and ENNReal.ofReal sends a real number t to the extended nonnegative real max(t,0); since r^2 is nonnegative, the Wasserstein bound compares against r^2 in the extended nonnegative reals.
